title: Bank Deposit Recall and Error-Notice Periods and the Listed Recall Fee
content:
Two remedies exist after a Bank Deposit payment has left Paloma: a recall, where the customer asks the beneficiary bank to send back a deposited payment that went to wrong details the customer supplied, and an error notice under the Remittance Transfer Rule. Each tier lists a recall fee and the periods that bound both.

| Tier | Listed recall fee (USD) | Recall period (calendar days after the deposit date) | Error-notice period (calendar days after the disclosed date of availability) | Paloma's decision period (calendar days after a notice) | Redelivery after a remedy choice (Paloma business days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bank Deposit Economy | 10.00 | 30 | 180 | 90 | 1 |
| Bank Deposit Standard | 10.00 | 30 | 180 | 90 | 1 |
| Bank Deposit Express | 10.00 | 10 | 180 | 90 | 1 |
| Bank Deposit Express Plus | 10.00 | 10 | 180 | 90 | 1 |
| Bank Deposit Large Amount | 15.00 | 60 | 180 | 90 | 1 |
| Bank Deposit International Wire | 35.00 | 180 | 180 | 90 | 1 |

## Definitions

- **Listed recall fee.** The fee a tier lists for asking the beneficiary bank to recall a deposited payment sent to wrong details the customer supplied.
- **Recall period.** The calendar days after the deposit date within which a recall may be requested.
- **Error-notice period.** The calendar days after the disclosed date of availability within which the customer may give notice of an error.
- **Decision period.** The calendar days after an error notice within which Paloma must decide it.
- **Redelivery time.** The Paloma business days within which funds are sent again after the customer chooses redelivery as a remedy.

## Reading the table

The error-notice, decision and redelivery figures are the same on every tier. The recall period is shortest on the real-time tiers (10 days) and longest on Bank Deposit International Wire (180 days), which also lists the highest recall fee, 35.00.
